# Run Analytics — AnalyticsZone

> Privacy-first running analytics for iOS and Apple Watch: Critical Running Speed (CRS), running training load (rTSS), and gait metrics computed locally on your device — no cloud uploads.

Run Analytics tracks Critical Running Speed, Training Stress Score, and performance metrics for runners, triathletes, and coaches. All metrics are based on peer-reviewed sports science and computed on-device.

## Key pages

- [Critical Running Speed (CRS)](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/crs/): The running equivalent of critical power — what it is and how to test it.
- [Training Load](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/training-load/): rTSS-based load, fitness, and fatigue for runners.
- [rTSS Calculator](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/rtss-calculator/): Interactive running Training Stress Score calculator.
- [Training Zones](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/training-zones/): Pace- and heart-rate-based running zones.
- [What is VO2max](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/what-is-vo2max/): VO2max explained for runners.
- [The 80/20 Training Rule](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/8020-training-rule/): Polarized intensity distribution in practice.
- [Gait Analysis for Runners](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/gait-analysis-runners/): Cadence, ground contact, and running form metrics.
- [Formulas](https://run.analyticszone.app/en/formulas/): Every formula the app uses, with references.

## Key facts

- Critical Running Speed (CRS) is the running analogue of critical power: the fastest metabolically sustainable pace, estimated from two maximal efforts of different durations.
- rTSS (running Training Stress Score) quantifies session load from duration and intensity relative to threshold pace.
- The 80/20 rule describes the intensity distribution observed in elite endurance runners: roughly 80% of sessions at low intensity, 20% at moderate-to-high intensity.
- All calculations run locally on the device; no training data is sent to any cloud.
